```plato
//==
// # Meshes polygon
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - MeshesPolygon — face and corner access for PolygonMesh3D
//  - Constructing and exporting PolygonMesh3D
//  - Half-edge navigation over PolygonMesh3D corners
//  - The IMeshIncidence rung for PolygonMesh3D

library MeshesPolygon
{
    //==
    // # MeshesPolygon — face and corner access for PolygonMesh3D
    //
    // PolygonMesh3D HAS a `JaggedArray<VertexIndex>` face table with one row per
    // face, so row arithmetic — RowCount / RowLength / Row / RowElement — comes from
    // `collections.library.plato` through `self.Faces` and is NOT restated
    // here. What this library adds is the mesh reading of those rows, and the one thing
    // the packing seam does not name: the CORNER.
    //
    // A corner is one vertex slot of one face, numbered globally by its position in
    // the packed values. That global corner number doubles as a half-edge
    // identifier — corner c is the directed edge from its own vertex to the next
    // corner of the same face — which is what lets the Conway operators run with no
    // side table at all. The navigation built on it follows in the sections below.

    //==
    // IMeshElementCounts obligations. VertexCount and FaceCount are direct reads;
    // UndirectedEdgeCount dedupes through the canonical-corner rule, so it holds
    // for open meshes as well as closed ones.

    // The number of positions the faces index into.
    VertexCount(self: PolygonMesh3D): Integer
        => self.Positions.Count;

    // The number of faces: one face-table row each.
    FaceCount(self: PolygonMesh3D): Integer
        => self.Faces.RowCount;

    // The number of undirected edges: one per canonical corner. An interior edge
    // is named by the lower half of its twin pair, a boundary edge by its only
    // corner, so no edge is double-counted and none is missed. The canonical rule
    // itself is `IsCanonicalCorner`, below.
    UndirectedEdgeCount(self: PolygonMesh3D): Integer
        => self.CornerCount
            .MapRange(c => self.IsCanonicalCorner(CornerIndex(c)) ? 1 : 0)
            .Reduce(0, (acc, hit) => acc + hit);

    //==
    // Corners: the global vertex slots, and the face-relative way in.

    // The total number of face corners across the whole mesh.
    CornerCount(self: PolygonMesh3D): Integer
        => self.Faces.Values.Count;

    // The number of vertices of a face. Precondition: 0 <= face < FaceCount.
    FaceArity(self: PolygonMesh3D, face: Integer): Integer
        => self.Faces.RowLength(face);

    // The corner at face f's slot-th vertex, wrapping around the face so
    // slot + 1 is always the next corner counter-clockwise.
    // Precondition: 0 <= face < FaceCount, slot >= 0.
    FaceCorner(self: PolygonMesh3D, face: Integer, slot: Integer): CornerIndex
        => CornerIndex(self.Faces.Offsets[face] + (slot % self.FaceArity(face)));

    // The vertex a corner refers to. Precondition: the corner is present.
    CornerVertex(self: PolygonMesh3D, corner: CornerIndex): VertexIndex
        => self.Faces.Values[corner.Value];

    // The position a corner refers to. Precondition: the corner is present.
    CornerPosition(self: PolygonMesh3D, corner: CornerIndex): Point3D
        => self.Positions[self.CornerVertex(corner).Value];

    //==
    // IWhole-face views. The vertex loop itself is `Faces.Row(face)`.

    // The positions of one face in counter-clockwise order.
    // Precondition: 0 <= face < FaceCount.
    FacePositions(self: PolygonMesh3D, face: Integer): Array<Point3D>
        => self.Faces.Row(face).Map(v => self.Positions[v.Value]);

    // The average of a face's vertex positions. Coincides with the area centroid
    // only for a regular face, which is exactly the polyhedral case the Conway
    // dual needs (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centroid).
    FaceCentroid(self: PolygonMesh3D, face: Integer): Point3D
        => self.FacePositions(face).AverageOfPoints;

    // Every face centroid, in face order: the vertex positions of the dual.
    FaceCentroids(self: PolygonMesh3D): Array<Point3D>
        => self.FaceCount.MapRange(f => self.FaceCentroid(f));

    // The IDeformable3D obligation: every vertex position carried through the
    // mapping, the face table unchanged.
    Deform(self: PolygonMesh3D, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): PolygonMesh3D
        => (self.Positions.Map(mapping), self.Faces);

    //==
    // # Constructing and exporting PolygonMesh3D
    //
    // The two directions the polygon mesh is crossed: IN from face vertex loops
    // (packed through `FromRows` in `collections.library.plato`, the one
    // place ragged rows become offsets) and OUT to the triangle-mesh interchange
    // form, plus the whole-mesh position maps the polyhedra seeds are stated with.
    //
    // Nothing here reads connectivity — that is the incidence section below.

    //==
    // Construction.

    // A polygon mesh from explicit face vertex loops, each wound
    // counter-clockwise seen from outside.
    // Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Winding, handedness, and normals.
    PolygonMeshOfFaces(positions: Array<Point3D>, faces: Array<Array<VertexIndex>>): PolygonMesh3D
        => (positions, FromRows(faces));

    // The same, from plain vertex numbers: the readable form for the literal
    // face tables of the polyhedra seeds.
    PolygonMeshOfVertexNumbers(positions: Array<Point3D>, faces: Array<Array<Integer>>): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMeshOfFaces(positions, faces.Map(face => face.Map(v => VertexIndex(v))));

    //==
    // IWhole-mesh position maps. Connectivity is untouched, so these are the
    // cheap way to place a mesh: the packing is shared, only positions differ.

    // Every vertex pushed out onto the unit sphere. For a polyhedron built from
    // a symmetric vertex table this is what makes the circumscribed radius
    // exactly one, and it is the canonical form the Conway operators return.
    ProjectedToUnitSphere(self: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => (self.Positions.Map(p => p.PositionVector.Normalize.ToPoint), self.Faces);

    // Every vertex scaled about the origin. Applied to a unit-sphere mesh this
    // sets the circumscribed radius.
    ScaledAboutOrigin(self: PolygonMesh3D, factor: Number): PolygonMesh3D
        => (self.Positions.Map(p => (p.PositionVector * factor).ToPoint), self.Faces);

    //==
    // Export.

    // One face fanned into triangles from its first vertex: (A, B, C),
    // (A, C, D), … — arity - 2 of them, and exact for a convex face
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fan_triangulation). Every catalog
    // polyhedron has convex faces; a non-convex face needs a real
    // triangulator instead.
    FaceTriangleFan(self: PolygonMesh3D, face: Integer): Array<TriangleFace>
        => (self.FaceArity(face) - 2).MapRange(i =>
            TriangleFace(self.CornerVertex(self.FaceCorner(face, 0)),
                         self.CornerVertex(self.FaceCorner(face, i + 1)),
                         self.CornerVertex(self.FaceCorner(face, i + 2))));

    // The IMesh3D obligation: fan every face, sharing the position array
    // unchanged so vertex numbering survives the conversion.
    ToTriangleMesh(self: PolygonMesh3D): TriangleMesh3D
        => (self.Positions,
            self.FaceCount.MapRange(f => f).FlatMap(f => self.FaceTriangleFan(f)));

    // The IMesh3D obligation of every IPolygonMesh3D: triangulate the polygon
    // mesh the type already knows how to produce.
    ToTriangleMesh(self: IPolygonMesh3D): TriangleMesh3D
        => self.ToPolygonMesh.ToTriangleMesh;
```
